skill.author: inference-sh-9

security_audit.summary: The audit confirmed the remote curl-to-shell installer and several executable infsh or npx examples as real command and network trust risks. Most other static hits are Markdown fences or inline identifiers and were false positives. A semantic risk remains because the voice and talking-head workflows lack consent and anti-impersonation guardrails.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into the shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell installation with a pinned download, checksum verification, and a manual execution step.

remediation.issue: External inference commands can send scripts and media URLs to remote services.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear confirmation guidance before sending private text, customer data, images, video URLs, or audio references.

remediation.issue: Voice and avatar workflows do not define consent or impersonation limits.
remediation.suggestion: Add rules requiring permission for real voices, portraits, likenesses, and identity-based synthetic media.

remediation.issue: Related-skill commands install additional packages or skills.
remediation.suggestion: Mark related installs as optional, pin versions where possible, and tell users to review each added skill separately.

content.value_statement: Synthetic voice production can be slow when every script needs recording and editing. This skill uses inference.sh voice models to create narration, dialogue, and voiceover audio from text.
actual_capabilities: Runs inference.sh TTS apps such as Kokoro, DIA, Chatterbox, Higgs, and VibeVoice.
Selects documented voices and pacing settings for narration, podcasts, and voiceovers.
Builds multi-speaker dialogue by generating separate audio tracks and merging them.
Supports long-form narration by chunking text and merging generated audio.
Combines generated speech with video or avatar workflows using media URLs.
limitations: Requires an installed and authenticated inference.sh CLI before commands can run.
Sends text, prompts, and media URLs to external inference.sh services.
Does not verify consent, rights, or identity authorization for voices, portraits, or scripts.
Output quality depends on selected model, voice, text length, and punctuation.

use_cases.title: Create Video Voiceovers
use_cases.description: Generate polished narration for product videos, tutorials, explainers, and social clips without booking a recording session.

use_cases.title: Produce Course Narration
use_cases.description: Turn lesson scripts into consistent spoken audio for e-learning modules, onboarding, and accessibility support.

use_cases.title: Draft Support Audio
use_cases.description: Create clear IVR prompts, help center audio, and short announcements with selected voices and controlled pacing.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Short Voiceover
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one script and one voice.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a warm 20-second voiceover from this text: [paste script]. Choose a suitable documented voice and keep the pacing natural.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Voice Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Choose a voice style before final production.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create short samples for this script using three suitable voices. Compare tone, clarity, and pacing, then recommend one voice.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Two-Speaker Dialogue
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a simple conversation with distinct speakers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a two-speaker conversation from this dialogue. Use different voices, keep each turn separate, and merge the final audio.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Long-Form Narration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for long scripts and consistent output.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this long script into narrated audio. Split it into logical chunks, keep one voice across all chunks, and merge the final result.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a 30-second product launch voiceover with an energetic but professional tone.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a clear professional voice, slightly faster pacing, and a short generated sample for review before final audio.

output_examples.input: A learning team needs narration for a five-minute onboarding lesson.
output_examples.output: The skill splits the script into smaller sections, keeps a consistent voice, and merges the generated audio into one lesson track.

output_examples.input: A creator wants a two-person podcast intro with host and guest voices.
output_examples.output: The skill assigns separate voices, generates each speaker turn, and combines the tracks with a short crossfade.

best_practices: Get consent before using any real person, portrait, voice likeness, or private script.
Test short samples before generating long audio so voice, speed, and punctuation can be adjusted.
Review all text for confidential information before sending it to external inference services.
anti_patterns: Creating voices or avatars that impersonate real people without clear permission.
Sending confidential scripts, customer data, or private media URLs without approval.
Using one very long prompt when chunking would improve consistency and recovery.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It generates synthetic speech, narration, dialogue, voiceovers, and related audio workflows through inference.sh apps.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require an external service?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses the inference.sh CLI and sends inputs to inference.sh services.

faq.question: Can it create multi-speaker audio?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill shows separate speaker generation and a merge step for conversation audio.

faq.question: Can it process long scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends splitting long text into chunks and merging the generated audio.

faq.question: What safety rules should users follow?
faq.answer: Users should avoid impersonation, confirm consent, and review sensitive text before using external services.
